raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Stacked on #48028 (`oss-sync-5cf60d009b`), which this pull request is opened against; only the top commit is this change. Review the two together or merge #48028 first.

## Motivation

`set_batch_invariant_mode()` snapshots the module globals on entry and assigns them back on exit. That is wrong whenever the scope starts with batch-invariant mode already enabled: `enable_batch_invariant_mode()` destroys the existing `torch.library.Library` and registers a fresh one, so the snapshot points at a destroyed library. On exit `_batch_invariant_MODE` reads `True` while the aten overrides (`mm`, `addmm`, `_log_softmax`, `mean.dim`, ...) are gone.

Concretely, with #48028 applied:

```python
enable_batch_invariant_mode()
with set_batch_invariant_mode(False):   # or a nested set_batch_invariant_mode()
    ...
# is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled() -> True, but torch.mm runs the default kernel
```

and a prior `enable_batch_invariant_mode(enable_bmm=False)` comes back with the Triton `bmm` patched in, because the inner enable defaulted `enable_bmm=True` and the snapshot cannot express "restore the previous registration".

## Modifications

- `set_batch_invariant_mode()` remembers two facts on entry: whether the mode was on, and whether `torch.bmm` was patched (`_original_torch_bmm is not None`).
- In `finally`, if either differs from the current state, it calls `disable_batch_invariant_mode()` and, when the mode was on before, `enable_batch_invariant_mode(enable_bmm=<previous>)`. State is restored through the same functions that build it, so the restored library is a live registration, `enable_bmm=False` round-trips, and an unchanged active registration is left alone.
- The enable/disable call moved inside the `try`, so a failure there also unwinds.
- New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops/test_batch_invariant_context.py` (registered to `base-a-test-cpu`, ~5 s). A fixture points the dispatcher at the CPU key with tiny CPU replacements (`a + b`) and checks `torch.mm`, `torch.bmm` and `torch.ops.aten.bmm.default` dispatch before, inside and after plain, failing, repeated and nested scopes, with `torch.bmm` patching on and off.

Behaviour inside the scope is unchanged; only what the scope leaves behind changes.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output changes. The new test is the regression check:

```
pytest test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops/test_batch_invariant_context.py -q
```

20 passed on this branch; on #48028 alone 16 of the 20 fail (every case that starts with the mode enabled or nests a scope). The existing `test_batch_invariant_ops.py` only enters the scope from a disabled state and is unaffected.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

files.patch:
@@ -1240,30 +1240,22 @@ def disable_batch_invariant_mode():
 
 @contextlib.contextmanager
 def set_batch_invariant_mode(enabled: bool = True):
-    global _batch_invariant_MODE, _batch_invariant_LIB, _original_torch_bmm
-    # enable_batch_invariant_mode() also replaces torch.bmm; restore it on exit,
-    # or every later torch.bmm in the process stays batch-invariant.
-    old_data = (
-        _batch_invariant_MODE,
-        _batch_invariant_LIB,
-        _original_torch_bmm,
-        torch.bmm,
-    )
-    if enabled:
-        enable_batch_invariant_mode()
-    else:
-        disable_batch_invariant_mode()
+    previous_mode = _batch_invariant_MODE
+    previous_bmm_enabled = _original_torch_bmm is not None
     try:
+        if enabled:
+            enable_batch_invariant_mode()
+        else:
+            disable_batch_invariant_mode()
         yield
     finally:
-        if _batch_invariant_LIB is not None:
-            _batch_invariant_LIB._destroy()
-        (
-            _batch_invariant_MODE,
-            _batch_invariant_LIB,
-            _original_torch_bmm,
-            torch.bmm,
-        ) = old_data
+        if (_batch_invariant_MODE, _original_torch_bmm is not None) != (
+            previous_mode,
+            previous_bmm_enabled,
+        ):
+            disable_batch_invariant_mode()
+            if previous_mode:
+                enable_batch_invariant_mode(enable_bmm=previous_bmm_enabled)
 
 
 AttentionBlockSize = namedtuple("AttentionBlockSize", ["block_m", "block_n"])

@@ -0,0 +1,94 @@
+import sys
+from contextlib import nullcontext
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.batch_invariant_ops import batch_invariant_ops as ops
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def native_bmm(monkeypatch):
+    was_enabled = ops.is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled()
+    had_bmm = ops._original_torch_bmm is not None
+    ops.disable_batch_invariant_mode()
+    original = torch.bmm
+    try:
+        with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
+            # Exercise real dispatcher registration with CPU-only replacements.
+            patch.setattr(ops, "get_dispatch_device_backend", lambda: "CPU")
+            patch.setattr(ops, "_is_npu", False)
+            patch.setattr(ops, "mm_batch_invariant", lambda a, b: a + b)
+            patch.setattr(ops, "bmm_batch_invariant", lambda a, b, *, out=None: a + b)
+            patch.setattr(torch, "bmm", original)
+            try:
+                yield original
+            finally:
+                ops.disable_batch_invariant_mode()
+    finally:
+        if was_enabled:
+            ops.enable_batch_invariant_mode(enable_bmm=had_bmm)
+
+
+def _assert_mode(enabled, enable_bmm, native_bmm):
+    assert ops.is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled() is enabled
+    assert torch.bmm is (ops.bmm_batch_invariant if enable_bmm else native_bmm)
+    a = torch.tensor([[2.0]], device="cpu")
+    b = torch.tensor([[3.0]], device="cpu")
+    assert torch.mm(a, b).item() == (5.0 if enabled else 6.0)
+    for bmm in (torch.bmm, torch.ops.aten.bmm.default):
+        assert bmm(a.unsqueeze(0), b.unsqueeze(0)).item() == (
+            5.0 if enable_bmm else 6.0
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("initial_bmm", [None, False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enabled", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("raises", [False, True])
+def test_scope_restores_dispatch(native_bmm, initial_bmm, enabled, raises):
+    was_enabled = initial_bmm is not None
+    if was_enabled:
+        ops.enable_batch_invariant_mode(enable_bmm=initial_bmm)
+    for _ in range(2):
+        with (
+            pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="scope failed")
+            if raises
+            else nullcontext()
+        ):
+            with ops.set_batch_invariant_mode(enabled):
+                _assert_mode(
+                    enabled,
+                    enabled and (initial_bmm if was_enabled else True),
+                    native_bmm,
+                )
+                if raises:
+                    raise RuntimeError("scope failed")
+        _assert_mode(was_enabled, bool(initial_bmm), native_bmm)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enable_bmm", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("inner_enabled", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("raises", [False, True])
+def test_nested_scope_preserves_outer_dispatch(
+    native_bmm, enable_bmm, inner_enabled, raises
+):
+    ops.enable_batch_invariant_mode(enable_bmm=enable_bmm)
+    with ops.set_batch_invariant_mode():
+        with (
+            pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="scope failed")
+            if raises
+            else nullcontext()
+        ):
+            with ops.set_batch_invariant_mode(inner_enabled):
+                _assert_mode(inner_enabled, inner_enabled and enable_bmm, native_bmm)
+                if raises:
+                    raise RuntimeError("scope failed")
+        _assert_mode(True, enable_bmm, native_bmm)
+    _assert_mode(True, enable_bmm, native_bmm)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
